requirements.goal: Answer research questions by finding sources on the web and writing a short cited summary that is saved to a local markdown file.
requirements.target_users: Students and analysts who want quick, sourced overviews.

root_agent.name: research_pipeline
root_agent.description: Runs source discovery and summary writing in order.

sub_agents.name: source_finder
sub_agents.description: Searches the web and lists the most relevant sources for the question.
sub_agents.instruction_outline:
- Turn the question into 2-3 search queries
- Call search_web for each
- Keep the 5 most relevant results with title, url and snippet

sub_agents.name: summary_writer
sub_agents.description: Writes a concise cited summary from the sources and saves it to disk.
sub_agents.instruction_outline:
- Read the sources from state
- Write a 150-250 word summary with numbered citations
- Save it with save_summary

tools.name: search_web
tools.description: Search the web and return titles, URLs and snippets.
tools.returns: dict with status and a list of results

tools.name: save_summary
tools.description: Save a markdown summary into the local summaries folder.

parameters.name: title
parameters.description: Summary title, used for the file name.

tools.returns: dict with status and the saved file path

inputs: A research question in plain text
outputs: A cited summary shown in chat and saved as markdown
guardrail_requirements: Only write files inside the summaries folder
acceptance_criteria: Given a question, source_finder stores at least three sources in state
summary_writer produces a summary that cites the stored sources
A markdown file appears in the summaries folder

agent_cards.instruction: You find sources for the user's research question. Turn the question into two or three short search queries and call search_web for each. Keep the five most relevant results. Reply with a numbered list: title, url and a one-line note on why it is relevant. Do not answer the question yourself and do not invent sources.
